quizzes.title: PSLV-C62 payloads: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: The PSLV-C62 flight carried a main satellite along with several other payloads. Among the passengers was EOS-N1, also called Anvesha, which is a satellite with an imaging instrument. A second payload, KID, was a vehicle built by a firm from abroad, and its job was to test how a small craft comes back through the atmosphere. Another payload, AayulSAT, came from a company based in Bengaluru and was among the technology demonstrations on the launch. Commercial customers from several countries also sent their satellites on the same flight, which made the list of passengers a long one. The rocket was set to lift off from Sriharikota in Andhra Pradesh. The mission followed an earlier setback in the same programme and was ISRO's first launch of the year 2026. The PSLV is a four-stage vehicle that was first launched in 1993 and uses solid propellants in its first and third stages and liquid propellants in its second and fourth stages. Its notable missions include Chandrayaan-1, the Mars Orbiter Mission and AstroSat. ISRO was formerly known as INCOSPAR and was renamed in 1969, and it is headquartered in Bengaluru. The Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System, known as NavIC, is another ISRO programme. Its payload capability is up to 1750 kg.

questions.q: What is the stated purpose of EOS-N1 (Anvesha)?
options: Strengthen space-based Earth observation and monitoring
questions.explanation: The booklet says EOS-N1 is meant to strengthen space-based Earth observation and monitoring.

questions.q: Which of these countries is among those whose commercial payloads flew on PSLV-C62?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists commercial payloads from India, Mauritius, Luxembourg, UAE, Singapore, Europe and the US.

questions.q: What does the acronym KID stand for?
questions.explanation: The booklet expands KID as Kestrel Initial Demonstrator.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): EOS-N1 was intended for a sun-synchronous orbit.
Reason (R): KID was developed by a Spanish startup.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the developer of KID does not explain the orbit intended for EOS-N1.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. EOS-N1 (Anvesha)   ->   A. Hyperspectral imaging satellite
II. AayulSAT   ->   B. India's 1st on-orbit satellite refuelling payload
III. KID developer   ->   C. Spanish startup
IV. KID mission   ->   D. Re-entry and splashdown in the South Pacific Ocean
questions.explanation: The booklet pairs EOS-N1 with hyperspectral imaging, AayulSAT with refuelling, KID with a Spanish startup, and KID's mission with splashdown in the South Pacific Ocean.

questions.q:
I. EOS-N1 (Anvesha) is a hyperspectral imaging satellite.
II. KID is a small-scale re-entry vehicle prototype.
III. AayulSAT was developed by a Spanish startup.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while AayulSAT was developed by Bengaluru-based OrbitAID Aerospace, not a Spanish startup.

questions.q:
I. AayulSAT is India's first on-orbit satellite refuelling payload.
II. KID's mission involved splashdown in the South Pacific Ocean.
III. EOS-N1 was developed by ISRO.
IV. AayulSAT is India's first weather satellite.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are in the booklet, while III and IV contradict it, since EOS-N1 was developed for DRDO's Strategic Applications and AayulSAT is a refuelling payload.

quizzes.title: PSLV-C62 payloads: typed answer practice
quizzes.passage: PSLV-C62 was a flight of the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, a rocket that ISRO calls its workhorse. The mission was planned for liftoff from Sriharikota, and it carried several payloads beyond its main satellite. One of these was EOS-N1, an imaging satellite that supports observation of the Earth from space. Another passenger was KID, a small prototype designed to return from space. KID was built by a startup from abroad. AayulSAT, a payload from a Bengaluru company, is a technology test linked to satellites that are already in orbit. Commercial customers from several countries also flew satellites on the mission. The PSLV is a medium-lift vehicle with a payload capability of up to 1750 kg, and its notable missions include Chandrayaan-1, the Mars Orbiter Mission and AstroSat. The Mars Orbiter Mission was the first Asian spacecraft to enter Martian orbit. ISRO is India's national space agency, and its headquarters are in Bengaluru. ISRO was formerly known as INCOSPAR and was renamed in 1969. The Indian Space Policy 2023 is the government's plan to let private enterprises carry out end-to-end activities. The Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System, known as NavIC, is another ISRO programme. The flight was ISRO's first launch in 2026, following a setback in the previous mission.

questions.q: What is the intended orbit type for EOS-N1? (orbit type)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the orbit intended for EOS-N1 as Sun Synchronous Orbit.

questions.q: In which ocean was KID's splashdown planned? (name of ocean)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives KID's mission as atmospheric re-entry and splashdown in the South Pacific Ocean.

questions.q: Which country's startup developed KID? (country)
questions.explanation: The booklet says KID was developed by a Spanish startup.

questions.q: What type of imaging does EOS-N1 perform? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes EOS-N1 as a hyperspectral imaging satellite.

questions.q: What kind of payload is AayulSAT, India's first of its kind on orbit? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet calls AayulSAT India's first on-orbit satellite refuelling payload.

questions.q: What is the term for KID's landing on the ocean, as stated for its mission? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says KID's mission ends with splashdown in the South Pacific Ocean.

questions.q: What is the name of the EOS-N1 satellite? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet identifies EOS-N1 as Anvesha.

quizzes.title: Launch vehicles and private players: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: India's launch vehicles come in several families, and each has its own role. Early rockets in the line came first, and newer designs followed. The Next Generation Launch Vehicle is a planned rocket, still in development, that is meant to carry much larger payloads than the current options. The NGLV is designed to be reusable and green. It is expected to enable missions such as human spaceflight. Another rocket, the Small Satellite Launch Vehicle, has flown test missions and is launched from Sriharikota. The SSLV is a three-stage vehicle, and its producing body is NSIL. Private companies have also started building rockets of their own. Agnikul Cosmos is one such company, and its rockets are launched from a privately developed launchpad. Its founders include Srinath Ravichandran, Moin SPM and Satya Chakravarthy, and its rocket is described as the world's first with a fully 3D-printed engine. The Indian Space Policy is the government's plan to let private enterprises take part in space activity. The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre, based in Ahmedabad, helps private players take part in space activity. ISRO, India's national space agency, is headquartered in Bengaluru. The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle, GSLV, has a Mk-III version that made ISRO entirely self-sufficient.

questions.q: Which launch vehicle is suited to launching multiple microsatellites and takes that load off the PSLV?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the SSLV is suited to launching multiple microsatellites and shifts that burden from the PSLV.

questions.q: What is the maximum payload capability of the NGLV?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the NGLV's maximum payload capability as 30 tonnes.

questions.q: What does SOrTeD, a demonstrator developed by Agnikul Cosmos, stand for?
questions.explanation: The booklet says SOrTeD stands for SubOrbital Technology Demonstrator.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): SSLV-D2 was a successful test flight.
Reason (R): SSLV-D1 ended in failure in 2022.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the 2022 failure of SSLV-D1 does not explain the later success of SSLV-D2.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. SLV   ->   A. ISRO's first satellite launch vehicle
II. GSLV   ->   B. Carries heavier satellites deeper into space
III. SSLV   ->   C. Suited to launching multiple microsatellites
IV. RHUMI-1   ->   D. India's first reusable hybrid rocket
questions.explanation: The booklet matches SLV with ISRO's first satellite launch vehicle, GSLV with deep-space payloads, SSLV with multiple microsatellites, and RHUMI-1 with India's first reusable hybrid rocket.

questions.q:
I. SLV was ISRO's first satellite launch vehicle, followed by ASLV.
II. NGLV has a maximum payload capability of 50 tonnes.
III. SSLV-D1 was a success in 2022.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I matches the booklet, since the NGLV's maximum payload is 30 tonnes and SSLV-D1 failed in 2022.

questions.q:
I. RHUMI-1 was developed by Space Zone India.
II. SOrTeD is a two-stage rocket.
III. Agnikul Cosmos was founded in 2010.
IV. The NGLV costs about three times as much as LVM3.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while Agnikul Cosmos was founded in 2017 and the NGLV costs 1.5 times LVM3.

quizzes.title: Launch vehicles and private players: typed answer practice
quizzes.passage: ISRO's rockets fall into different families, and each has its own role. The SLV was ISRO's first satellite launch vehicle, and the ASLV followed it. The GSLV has a Mk-III version that made ISRO self-sufficient, and it is meant to carry heavier satellites deeper into space. The SSLV is one of the smaller members of that family, and its test flights have shown what it can do. The SSLV is a three-stage vehicle, and its launch site is Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota. The SSLV is produced by NSIL. The NGLV is a much larger rocket that is still being planned, with a big payload target, and it is designed to be reusable and green. On the private side, Agnikul Cosmos works on launch systems and uses a launchpad of its own. Agnikul Cosmos was founded by three people, including Srinath Ravichandran, and its engine is described as the world's first fully 3D-printed one. Another private effort is a rocket of a different design that was launched with a partner group and carried a few small satellites. The Indian Space Policy is the government's plan that opens space activity to private firms. ISRO is India's national space agency, and its headquarters are in Bengaluru.

questions.q: In which year did SSLV-D2 succeed? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says that with SSLV-D2 in 2023, ISRO tasted success.

questions.q: What does the acronym ASLV stand for?
questions.explanation: The booklet names ASLV as the Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle that followed the SLV.

questions.q: What is the name of the launchpad used by Agnikul Cosmos? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives Dhanush as the launch site and describes it as India's first privately developed launchpad.

questions.q: In which year was Agnikul Cosmos founded? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Agnikul Cosmos was founded in 2017.

questions.q: What is the maximum payload capability of the NGLV? (in tonnes)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the NGLV's maximum payload capability as 30 tonnes.

questions.q: What is the name of India's first reusable hybrid rocket? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet identifies RHUMI-1 as India's first reusable hybrid rocket, developed by Space Zone India.

questions.q: Agnikul Cosmos was the first company in India to sign an agreement with ISRO under which scheme? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Agnikul was the first company in India to sign an agreement with ISRO under IN-SPACe.
